searchText: Intersting! I do think that realistically, if we're going anywhere at all we're going verkle at this point The reasoning is that with some recent analyses of concrete impacts of introducing code chunk gas cost, we're already brushing up against a hard wall in terms of the tradeoff between bounding witness size and not overcharging existing applications A cost of 200 gas per chunk (~6.25 gas per witness byte) increases *average* gas usage by ~25% So anything that has more-than-negligible overhead per code chunk is outright unviable, unfortunately The implementation work by <@!425343240212971521> and <@!259648573401071617> was done Q1, before most of the verkle tree work commenced. The goal was to share the results, even if it may not be used. I think the actual chunking implementation can be used for verkle too, but not sure if the ssz proofs can be reused in any form. Got it, thanks for the context! x-post from <#688075293562503241>: > Dedaub just published an analysis of the impact of verkle trie gas metering: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1s3qqzbkQFPcNvhzKPdnxg3MlFbv0YjK1z02SxRtdMs8/edit > > I think it could be good to organize a stateless ethereum call in the next week or two for the team to present the results and answer questions. Sent them an invite for the discord 🙂
